# Zoé

> HTML-first web components with living states (`:state()`), portable skins (one CSS file of tokens) and CSS-driven motion. Light DOM, zero dependencies, 36 components, 10 tools, 2 skins. Version 0.9.0, generated 2026-10-14.

This file is generated by `scripts/z-manifest` from the source code. Machine-readable twins: `dist/zoe.json` (full index), `dist/custom-elements.json` (Custom Elements Manifest), `dist/vscode.html-custom-data.json`. An MCP server exposes the same data: `node scripts/z-mcp/z-mcp.js` (see `.mcp.json`).

---

# Zoé — the grammar

> The complete rule set for writing Zoé. One page. Everything else (the generated
> manifest, `llms.txt`, the MCP server) is derived from the same source as this page:
> the `static api` block of each element and the CSS it ships with.

Zoé extends HTML with **custom elements** that carry **interaction states**
(`:state()`), are **painted by a skin** (one CSS file of tokens) and **move** (every
state change is animatable). Everything lives in the **light DOM**: the author's HTML
stays the author's HTML, Zoé never injects a node.

## 1. Loading

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/zoe.css">                      <!-- the library -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/skins/hightech/hightech.css">  <!-- one skin, last -->
<script type="module" src="/zoe.js"></script>                <!-- every element -->
```

Only one component needed? Import its module alone: `components/z-button/z-button.js`.
Pages must be served over HTTP (`npm run dev`): ES modules do not load from `file://`.

## 2. Writing an element

**Short form** — the CSS paints the host. One line, nothing to learn:

```html
<z-checkbox>Receive the newsletter</z-checkbox>
```

**Layered form** — each piece is a `<z-layer part="…">`, so each piece can move on its
own. The author writes the layers; Zoé never generates them (ADR-0018):

```html
<z-checkbox>
  <z-layer part="background"></z-layer>
  <z-layer part="marker">
    <z-layer part="ring"></z-layer>
    <z-layer part="dot"></z-layer>
  </z-layer>
  <z-layer part="infos">
    <z-layer part="label">Receive the newsletter</z-layer>
  </z-layer>
  <z-layer part="contact"></z-layer>
</z-checkbox>
```

Both forms read the same tokens and behave the same. Each component declares **its own
anatomy** (the `layers` of its API). The **lexicon is shared**: `background`, `marker`,
`ring`, `dot`, `infos`, `icon`, `label`, `contact` mean the same thing in every
component — never invent a synonym for an existing role, and never name a part after a
CSS property (`part="border"` is forbidden; the piece is `ring`).

Universal roles and their placement (`core/z-layer/z-layer.css`):

| part | role | placement |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | the surface behind everything | absolute, `z-index: 0`, may bleed |
| `marker` | the piece that shows state (box, dot, fill, track) | in flow, holds its place |
| `ring` · `dot` | pieces of the marker | anchored inside `marker` |
| `infos` | what informs — groups `icon` + `label` | inline-flex |
| `contact` | what receives the gesture — invisible, may overflow | absolute, `z-index: 10` |

## 3. States — `z-x:state(name)`

Every Zoé element poses its states itself through `ElementInternals.states`. One
selector form, no exception, no "is this one native?" list:

```css
z-button:state(over)    { … }
z-button:state(press)   { … }
z-button:state(current) { … }
```

| state | kind | when |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | rest | no status is active |
| `over` | transient | pointer is on the element |
| `press` | transient | pointer is down (held even if it leaves — pointer capture) |
| `release` | transient | pointer released **inside** — the gesture succeeds |
| `releaseOut` | transient | pointer released **outside** — the gesture is cancelled |
| `drag` | transient | pressed and moved beyond 4 px |
| `focus` | transient | keyboard focus (like `:focus-visible`) |
| `enter` | transient | just mounted — the entrance animation |
| `exit` | transient | played by whoever removes the element (`await el.play("exit")`) |
| `current` | durable | selected: checked box, active tab, chosen radio |
| `select` · `unselect` | transient | played automatically when `current` toggles |
| `loading` · `disabled` · `error` · `success` | durable status | set by attribute or `setState()` |
| `from-<status>` | transient | sequence: `:state(success):state(from-loading)` |

**Durable states are attributes.** `<z-button loading>` ⟺ `btn.setState("loading")`
⟺ `z-button:state(loading)`. The attribute is the source of truth. A component adds its
own (`indeterminate`, `open`, `held`…) — they are listed in its API.

**Declarative triggers** — `state="name: condition, …"`:

```html
<z-element state="armed: press +2s, glow: over, busy">…</z-element>
```

`armed` turns on 2 s after the press, `glow` on hover, `busy` immediately. Conditions
are a gesture (any state of the element, optional `+delay`) or a clock (`every 2s`).

**CSS can declare a state**: `@property --z-state__glow {}` → Zoé discovers it, and
`<z-element glow>` / `:state(glow)` work.

Transient durations are read from the cascade: `--z-dur-release`, `--z-dur-enter`,
`--z-dur-exit`… One source for the JS timer and the CSS animation.

## 4. Variants — `size · tone · width`

Pure CSS attributes available on every element:

| attribute | values |
|---|---|
| `size` | `xs` · `s` · `m` (default) · `l` · `xl` — one factor on `font-size`; everything inside is in `em` and follows |
| `tone` | `main` (default) · `complement` · `soft` · `success` · `danger` — sets `--z-tone__fill/ink/line` |
| `width` | `auto` (default) · `full` |

## 5. Painting — the pact

```
--z-{component}[--{part}]__{css-property}      what you paint
z-{component}:state({state})                   when
```

- `--` (double dash) is the **component → part** boundary; `__` is the **subject →
  property** boundary; single `-` joins words inside a name. Boundaries are doubled,
  words stay simple — the name is machine-deducible.
- `{css-property}` is the **exact CSS name**, never abbreviated: `background-color`,
  not `bg`.
- Omit the part when the property has a natural layer: `--z-button__color` paints the
  text, `--z-button--marker__background` paints the marker's fill.

```css
z-button                  { --z-button__background-color: #2d6cdf; }
z-button:state(press)     { --z-button__background-color: #1b4fb0; }
z-checkbox:state(current) { --z-checkbox--marker__background-checked: #ff2d55; }
```

**A state redefines a swatch**; everything that drinks the swatch follows, and the
override stays local (it descends into the element, never leaks to siblings or parents).

Component CSS consumes tokens with a fallback to the **skin's global tokens**:
`var(--z-button__background-color, var(--z-accent))`. Two levels, two names: a global
token (`--z-accent`) is never also a component variable.

**Targeting a piece** — direct child, by role, from the component:

```css
z-checkbox:has(z-layer):state(current) > z-layer[part="marker"] > z-layer[part="dot"] { scale: 1; }
```

- `>` keeps a nested component from being repainted by its parent's CSS.
- `:has(z-layer)` / `:not(:has(z-layer))` is the switch between layered and short form.
- `::part()` does **not** apply: Zoé is light DOM. Use `> [part=…]`.

## 6. Skins

A skin is **one CSS file of tokens** on `:root`, plus optional per-component overrides
and the classless layer that dresses native HTML (`article`, `form`…). Switching skin =
switching one `<link>`. The global vocabulary every skin provides:

```
--z-page --z-surface --z-surface-raised --z-surface-sunken      surfaces
--z-ink --z-ink-soft --z-line --z-line-soft                       ink & rules
--z-accent --z-accent-ink --z-accent-soft --z-focus-halo         the accent
--z-success --z-danger --z-disabled                              meaning
--z-font --z-font-title --z-font-size --z-font-size-sm           type
--z-font-weight --z-font-weight-strong --z-letter
--z-radius --z-radius-pill --z-border-width --z-gap --z-pad-x --z-pad-y
--z-dur --z-dur-enter --z-dur-exit --z-dur-release --z-dur-releaseOut
--z-dur-select --z-dur-unselect --z-dur-open --z-dur-close
--z-ease --z-ease-spring
--z-scale-base --z-scale-xs --z-scale-s --z-scale-m --z-scale-l --z-scale-xl
--z-contact-fx --z-contact-size --z-contact-width --z-contact-duration --z-contact-color
```

Each state also exposes `--z-state__color` (accent at rest, danger on `error`, success
on `success`, disabled when `disabled`): paint halos and rings with it and they stay in
tune without a line.

## 7. Tools

Tools apply to any HTML, Zoé element or not.

- **`<z-contact>`** — one tag anywhere in the page, and every interactive element gets
  the skin's click effect at the pointer position. `fx="none"` to disable.
- **`channel="name"`** — elements sharing a channel are linked: the emitter's value
  lands on every member as `--z-channel-name` (a bare number). Multi-output components
  split with the pact's separator: `--z-channel-name--low`. `Zoe.tune(name, value)`
  writes from JS.
- **Sensors** — they paint nothing and pose **bare numbers** on themselves, inherited by
  every descendant: `<z-pointer>` (`--z-pointer--local__x/__y/__rx/__ry/__in`),
  `<z-scroll>` (`--z-scroll__ry` 0→1, `__y`, `__dir`, `__top`, `__end`…), `<z-inview>`
  (`--z-inview__in`, `__ratio`, `__seen`, `__cross`), `<z-size>` (`--z-size__w`, `__h`,
  `__ratio`, `__over`), `<z-drag>` (`--z-drag__x/__y/__rx/__ry`, `__held`,
  `:state(held)`). Multiply a number to turn it into anything: `calc(var(--x) * 1px)`,
  `* 360deg`, `* 100%`.
- **`z-motion`** — shared `@keyframes`: `pop`, `shake`, `pulse`, `spin`, `fadeIn/Out`,
  `slideUp/Down/Left/Right` (+ `slideOut*`), `shimmer`, `ripple`.
- **`<z-cursor>`** — a ribbon following the pointer, skinned by the skin.

## 8. Events and JS

HTML first: no JS is required for an element to exist. When needed:

```js
const box = document.querySelector("z-checkbox");
box.addEventListener("change", () => box.checked);
box.addEventListener("z-state", (e) => e.detail);   // { states, changed, on }
box.setState("loading"); box.setState("loading", false);
await box.play("exit"); box.remove();                // animated removal
```

Component events (`change`, `input`, `toggle`, `select`, `zoe:dismiss`, `zoe:remove`…)
bubble and, where it makes sense, are cancelable. A component **emits, the page decides**:
zero business logic inside a component. Security is server-side.

## 9. Forms

Every Zoé input is form-associated: `name`, `value`, `required`, `disabled` (also via
`<fieldset disabled>`), native validation and `form.reset()` work as on native inputs.
Submission uses `FormData` as usual. A `<z-field>` wraps a **native** `<input>`,
`<textarea>` or `<select>` and mirrors its validity into `error` / `success`.

## 10. SEO contract

**Read by search engines → native HTML, dressed by the skin. Clicked → `z-*`.**
Headings, paragraphs, links, images, lists stay native. Only widgets (buttons, tabs,
dialogs, sliders) become Zoé elements. Never generate semantics from JS
(`<z-text h1>` is wrong; `<h1>` inside `<z-reveal>` is right).

## 11. Dead forms — never write these

| wrong | why | right |
|---|---|---|
| `.z-press`, `.is-over` | states are not classes | `z-x:state(press)` |
| `[state="press"]` | an element is `over` **and** `press` at once | `:state(press)` |
| `--z-button-bg`, `--z-button--bg` | abbreviation; single dash as boundary | `--z-button__background-color` |
| `--z__color` | leaks into children by inheritance | `--z-button__color` |
| `--z-button__color--press` | state suffix | `z-button:state(press) { --z-button__color: … }` |
| `role="marker"` | `role` belongs to ARIA | `part="marker"` |
| `<z-marker>`, `<z-label>` | a tag per role — a dictionary, not a grammar | `<z-layer part="marker">` |
| `::part(label)` | shadow-DOM only; Zoé is light DOM | `> [part=label]` |
| `part="border"` | a CSS property, not a role | `part="ring"` |
| `busy` | a second word for `loading` | `loading` |

## 12. Checklist for a generated page

1. `zoe.css` + one skin + `zoe.js` (or the needed modules).
2. Semantic content in native HTML; widgets as `z-*`.
3. Attributes from the element's API only (see `llms.txt` / `zoe_get`).
4. Paint with `--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`; react with `:state()`.
5. One `<z-contact>` if the page wants the skin's click effect.
6. Serve over HTTP; load `tools/z-lint/z-lint.js` in development — unknown tags,
   attributes, states and misspelled tokens are reported in the console with the
   nearest valid name.

---

# Reference

## core

### <z-element>

The living base: carries interaction states as :state() and emits z-state.

```html
<z-element state="glow: over">
  <button>Envoyer</button>
</z-element>
<style>
  z-element:state(press) > button { scale: .97; }
  z-element:state(glow)  > button { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--z-accent-soft); }
</style>
```

Attributes:
- `current` (boolean) — Durable selection (checked, active tab) — set by a selectable component.
- `loading` (boolean) — Status: loading / processing.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: blocks interaction.
- `error` (boolean) — Status: error.
- `success` (boolean) — Status: valid / done.
- `name` (string) — Form field name — used only by components that submit a value.
- `required` (boolean) — The form is invalid until this control has a value.
- `state` (enum) [état: condition, …] — `état: condition, …`: custom states, each with an optional condition — state="armed: press +2s, glow: over, busy". Comma separates; `:` adds a condition (gesture like `press +2s`, or clock `every 2s`); no condition = posed at once.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-element:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-dur-enter` — Duration of the transient `enter` state (read from the cascade).
- `--z-dur-release` — Duration of the `release` ripple.

JS API:
- `setState(name, on = true)` : void — Sets or clears a state. A durable or CSS-declared state goes through its attribute; any other name is posed directly in :state().
- `toggleState(name)` : void — Flips a state.
- `play(word)` : Promise<void> — Plays a transient state and resolves when it ends (duration read from --z-dur-<word>). `await el.play("exit")` before `el.remove()`.
- `states` : string[] — The states active right now.
- `disabled` : boolean — Read-only mirror of the `disabled` attribute.
- `setFormValue(value)` : void — What the element submits in its form; `null` submits nothing (components call it, pages rarely do).
- `setValidity(message?)` : void — Declares the element invalid with a message, or valid without one.
- `checkValidity() · reportValidity()` : boolean — The standard constraint-validation API, as on a native input.

Files: doc: core/z-element/z-element.doc.md

### <z-layer>

The pieces of a component — its background, its label, its tick — already painted for you. You only write a layer to take over one precise part.

```html
<z-checkbox>
  <z-layer part="background"></z-layer>
  <z-layer part="marker">
    <z-layer part="ring"></z-layer>
    <z-layer part="dot"></z-layer>
  </z-layer>
  <z-layer part="infos">
    <z-layer part="label">J'accepte les conditions</z-layer>
  </z-layer>
  <z-layer part="contact"></z-layer>
</z-checkbox>
```

Attributes:
- `part` (string) — The role this layer plays (background, marker, ring, dot, label, icon…). Shared across components: the same word means the same thing everywhere.

States (`z-layer:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-layer--background__bleed`, `--z-layer--contact__bleed`, `--z-layer--infos__gap`

Files: doc: core/z-layer/z-layer.doc.md

## tools

### z-channel

The channel: two elements sharing the same channel="name" are linked. What changes here moves there — and the CSS decides what. No class, no listener.

```html
<input type="range" channel="tempo" min="0" max="100" value="40">
<div channel="tempo" style="height: 8px; background: var(--z-accent); width: calc(var(--z-channel-tempo) * 1%)"></div>
```

Attributes:
- `channel` (string) — This element's channel name(s), space-separated (channel="x y"). The subscription IS the attribute: adding it joins, removing it leaves.

CSS variables:
- `--z-channel-{nom}` — Set by the tool on every member: the channel's current value. Read it in CSS — calc(var(--z-channel-tempo) * 1%).
- `--z-channel-{nom}--{part}` — When the source has several outputs (a z-range: low/high), one variable per part, using the pact's double separator.

JS API:
- `tune(name, value)` : void — Exported function — writes a value on a channel from JS (a server, a clock); every member follows.

Files: doc: tools/z-channel/z-channel.doc.md · lab: tools/z-channel/z-channel.lab.html

### <z-contact>

Need a click effect across your whole page? Drop this tag anywhere — problem solved. Two effects by default; not to your taste? Make your own in a few lines of CSS.

```html
<z-contact></z-contact>
<!-- one tag anywhere in the page: every interactive element gets the skin's click effect -->
```

Attributes:
- `fx` (enum) [none] — Kill switch only; the effect itself belongs to the skin. — `none`: cut the effect on this page — fx's ONLY role. WHICH effect shows belongs to the skin, never the page
- `disabled` (boolean) — Set by the engine on every source but the last one — the last declared wins.
- `size` (enum) [<longueur>] — `<longueur>`: e.g. 24px — sets --z-contact-size
- `width` (enum) [<longueur>] — `<longueur>`: e.g. 2px — sets --z-contact-width
- `duration` (enum) [<durée>] — `<durée>`: e.g. 2s — sets --z-contact-duration
- `color` (enum) [<couleur>] — `<couleur>`: e.g. tomato — sets --z-contact-color

Events: `zoe:contact` — Emitted on the touched target. detail: { fx, x, y, size, duration, pointerType }.

CSS variables:
- `--z-contact-size` — The size of the effect.
- `--z-contact-width` — Thickness of the outline.
- `--z-contact-duration` — Duration of the effect.
- `--z-contact-color` — Colour — defaults to the accent of the touched element.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-contact--target__w`, `--z-contact__fx`, `--z-contact__release`

Files: doc: tools/z-contact/z-contact.doc.md · lab: tools/z-contact/z-contact.lab.html

### <z-cursor>

The pointer's wake: one flat tag, and the mouse leaves a ribbon behind it.

```html
<z-cursor fx="move" tone="main"></z-cursor>
```

Attributes:
- `fx` (string) — move (the ribbon follows the mouse, default) · click (it fuses from one click to the next) · none.
- `tone` (string) — Colours the wake with the tone (main · complement · soft).
- `size` (string) — Thickness of the wake, on the shared scale (xs → xl).

States (`z-cursor:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-trail-thickness` — Head thickness (px).
- `--z-trail-scale` — Multiplies the thickness — what the `size` attribute sets.
- `--z-trail-fade` — Life of a point (ms) — the wake's length.
- `--z-trail-smooth` — Follow smoothness: low = it trails, 1 = glued to the pointer.
- `--z-trail-speed-ref` — Mouse speed (px/ms) that fills the head.
- `--z-trail-speed-fuse` — Speed (px/ms) of the trip from one click to the next.
- `--z-trail-ease` — Head→tail falloff: linear quad cubic quart quint expo sine back.
- `--z-trail-color` — Colour (defaults to the skin's accent).

Files: doc: tools/z-cursor/z-cursor.doc.md · demo: tools/z-cursor/z-cursor.demo.html

### <z-drag>

Dragging is the single biggest pile of JavaScript in any interface. Wrap it in this tag: the position lands in CSS as a number, and YOU decide what it moves — a position, a rotation, an opacity. Keyboard included.

```html
<z-drag axis="x" bounds>
  <div class="knob"></div>
</z-drag>
<style>
  .knob { width: 2em; height: 2em; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--z-accent); cursor: grab;
          translate: calc(var(--z-drag__x) * 1px) 0; scale: calc(1 + var(--z-drag__held) * .1); }
  z-drag:state(held) .knob { cursor: grabbing; }
</style>
```

Attributes:
- `axis` (enum) [x | y] — Locks the gesture to one axis. Optional: reading only __x in your CSS already gives a horizontal slider — this attribute exists so the GESTURE itself refuses the other direction, which is what a finger feels. — `x`: horizontal only · `y`: vertical only
- `bounds` (boolean) — Keeps the object inside its parent, and turns on __rx / __ry — the share travelled, 0→1. Without it the object goes wherever the hand goes.

Events: `zoe:drop` — Emitted on release — the only moment a page has something to do. detail: { x, y, rx, ry }.

States (`z-drag:state(…)`): `held`
- `held` — z-drag:state(held) while the object is held. It doubles the token, and neither covers the other: a selector switches (a cursor, a z-index), a number interpolates (a scale, a shadow).

CSS variables:
- `--z-drag__x` — The position along X, in pixels from the starting point — a bare number, so multiply it into whatever you want moved.
- `--z-drag__y` — The position along Y, in pixels from the starting point.
- `--z-drag__rx` — With bounds: the share travelled horizontally, 0→1 — a slider's value, for free.
- `--z-drag__ry` — With bounds: the share travelled vertically, 0→1.
- `--z-drag__held` — 1 while the object is held, 0 once let go — for the shadow that lifts under the finger.

Files: doc: tools/z-drag/z-drag.doc.md · lab: tools/z-drag/z-drag.lab.html

### <z-inview>

"Fade it in when it scrolls into view" — the single most common request on the web, and the reason whole libraries get loaded. Wrap it in this tag: the answer arrives in CSS as a number, and the animation stays yours to write.

```html
<z-inview>
  <h2>Ce titre entre en scène</h2>
</z-inview>
<style>
  z-inview h2 { opacity: var(--z-inview__seen); translate: 0 calc((1 - var(--z-inview__seen)) * 20px);
                transition: opacity .6s, translate .6s; }
</style>
```

Attributes:
- `margin` (string) [<longueur>] — Grows or shrinks the screen for this element only. A negative value waits until it is well inside; a positive one prepares it before it arrives. — `<longueur>`: e.g. -80px — trigger later, once it is really in view

CSS variables:
- `--z-inview__in` — 1 as soon as a single pixel is on screen, 0 otherwise — for what should play again at every pass.
- `--z-inview__ratio` — The visible share of the element, 0→1. It saturates at 1 once the element fits entirely on screen.
- `--z-inview__seen` — 1 once seen — and it NEVER goes back down. An entrance does not replay: this is the number that stops a page from making you dizzy on the way back up.
- `--z-inview__cross` — The crossing of the screen: 0 entering from the bottom, 1 leaving through the top. The number that keeps moving when ratio has saturated — for a decor that drifts the whole way through.

Files: doc: tools/z-inview/z-inview.doc.md · lab: tools/z-inview/z-inview.lab.html

### z-lint

The console that corrects: load it in development and every unknown tag, attribute, state, part or misspelled token is reported with the nearest valid name. The browser stays silent; z-lint speaks.

```html
<script type="module" src="tools/z-lint/z-lint.js"></script>
```

Events: `zoe:lint` — Fired on `document` after each pass. detail: { findings } — each finding has level, kind, found, expected, message.

JS API:
- `ZoeLint.lint()` : Promise<object[]> — Re-runs the analysis on the whole page and returns the findings (also printed to the console).

Files: doc: tools/z-lint/z-lint.doc.md · lab: tools/z-lint/z-lint.lab.html

### z-motion

Shared @keyframes presets — attach them to any state: `animation: pop var(--z-dur) var(--z-ease)`.

```html
z-button:state(error) { animation: shake var(--z-dur) var(--z-ease); }
```

Presets: `offerts`, `R`, `slideLeft`, `slideRight`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `slideOutLeft`, `slideOutRight`, `slideOutUp`, `slideOutDown`, `pop`, `shake`, `pulse`, `spin`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`, `shimmer`, `ripple`

Files: doc: tools/z-motion/z-motion.doc.md · lab: tools/z-motion/z-motion.lab.html

### <z-pointer>

Want a div to follow the mouse? Wrap it in this tag — the position lands in CSS as plain numbers, and every child inherits them. No class, no listener, no JS of yours.

```html
<z-pointer>
  <div class="halo"></div>
</z-pointer>
<style>
  .halo {
    position: absolute; width: 200px; height: 200px; margin: -100px 0 0 -100px; border-radius: 50%;
    background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--z-accent), transparent 70%);
    translate: calc(var(--z-pointer--local__x) * 1px) calc(var(--z-pointer--local__y) * 1px);
    opacity: var(--z-pointer--local__in);
  }
</style>
```

Attributes:
- `local` (boolean) — Coordinates in the BOX's frame (0,0 = its top-left corner). Taken by default when no frame is asked for — it is the common case, and the cheapest.
- `global` (boolean) — Coordinates in the WINDOW's frame (0,0 = its top-left corner). The pointer is then followed everywhere, even outside the box — useful for a crosshair or a page-wide light.

CSS variables:
- `--z-pointer--local__x` — Distance from the box's left edge, in pixels — a bare number, so multiply it (* 1px).
- `--z-pointer--local__y` — Distance from the box's top edge, in pixels.
- `--z-pointer--local__rx` — The share of the box crossed horizontally, 0→1 — becomes an angle (* 360deg), a share (* 100%), anything.
- `--z-pointer--local__ry` — The share of the box crossed vertically, 0→1.
- `--z-pointer--local__in` — 1 while the pointer is inside the box, 0 outside — the switch a skin uses to fade a halo out cleanly.
- `--z-pointer--global__x` — Distance from the window's left edge, in pixels.
- `--z-pointer--global__y` — Distance from the window's top edge, in pixels.
- `--z-pointer--global__rx` — The share of the window crossed horizontally, 0→1.
- `--z-pointer--global__ry` — The share of the window crossed vertically, 0→1.

Files: doc: tools/z-pointer/z-pointer.doc.md · lab: tools/z-pointer/z-pointer.lab.html

### <z-scroll>

A progress bar, a shrinking header, a parallax, a "back to top" that waits its turn — all of them need one thing: how far down are we? Drop this tag and the answer lands in CSS as a number between 0 and 1.

```html
<z-scroll page></z-scroll>
<div class="progress"></div>
<style>
  .progress { position: fixed; inset: 0 auto auto 0; height: 3px; background: var(--z-accent);
              width: calc(var(--z-scroll__ry) * 100%); }
</style>
```

Attributes:
- `page` (boolean) — Measure the PAGE's scroll instead of this box. The numbers are then set on :root, readable everywhere — the page's scroll belongs to no one in particular.

CSS variables:
- `--z-scroll__ry` — The share scrolled vertically, 0 at the start, 1 at the end — the number that serves 90% of the time.
- `--z-scroll__rx` — The share scrolled horizontally, 0→1.
- `--z-scroll__y` — The distance scrolled vertically, in pixels — a bare number, so multiply it (* 1px).
- `--z-scroll__x` — The distance scrolled horizontally, in pixels.
- `--z-scroll__dir` — 1 going down, -1 going up. It keeps its last value at rest — the one number you can never get otherwise, since it needs the previous position.
- `--z-scroll__top` — 1 while nothing has moved from the start — for a header that only shrinks once you leave the top.
- `--z-scroll__end` — 1 when the end is reached — for the shadow that fades out once there is nothing left to see.

Files: doc: tools/z-scroll/z-scroll.doc.md · lab: tools/z-scroll/z-scroll.lab.html

### <z-size>

Two questions CSS cannot answer on its own: how big is this box, really — and does its content overflow? Wrap it in this tag and both answers land in CSS as numbers.

```html
<z-size>
  <p>Ce texte grandit avec sa boîte.</p>
</z-size>
<style>
  z-size p { font-size: calc(14px + var(--z-size__w) * 0.012px); }
  z-size   { box-shadow: inset 0 calc(var(--z-size__over) * -8px) 8px -8px var(--z-ink-soft); }
</style>
```

CSS variables:
- `--z-size__w` — The inner width, in pixels — a bare number, so multiply it. This is what container queries never give you: a value to interpolate.
- `--z-size__h` — The inner height, in pixels.
- `--z-size__ratio` — Width divided by height. Above 1 it is lying down, below 1 it is standing up — one number to swap a layout on shape rather than on size.
- `--z-size__over` — 1 if the content overflows on either side. THE question CSS has no answer for — and the reason so many edge shadows and "see more" arrows mean nothing.
- `--z-size__over-x` — 1 if the content overflows horizontally.
- `--z-size__over-y` — 1 if the content overflows vertically.

Files: doc: tools/z-size/z-size.doc.md · lab: tools/z-size/z-size.lab.html

## components

### <z-accordion>

A group of z-disclosure — when `exclusive`, opening one closes the others. Coordination only.

```html
<z-accordion exclusive>
  <z-disclosure open>
    <z-layer part="label">Livraison</z-layer>
    <z-layer part="panel">Sous 48 h en France métropolitaine.</z-layer>
  </z-disclosure>
  <z-disclosure>
    <z-layer part="label">Retours</z-layer>
    <z-layer part="panel">30 jours, sans justificatif.</z-layer>
  </z-disclosure>
</z-accordion>
```

Attributes:
- `exclusive` (boolean) — Only one disclosure open at a time — opening one closes the others.

Events: `toggle` — Bubbles from the disclosure that opened or closed; the group has already closed the others if exclusive. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-accordion:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-accordion__gap` — Space between the stacked disclosures.

JS API:
- `exclusive` : boolean — Mirrors the `exclusive` attribute.
- `disclosures` : Element[] — The z-disclosure children this accordion coordinates.

Files: doc: components/z-accordion/z-accordion.doc.md · demo: components/z-accordion/z-accordion.demo.html

### <z-alert>

A contextual message — tone drives the colour, role=status (or alert for danger). Optionally dismissible.

```html
<z-alert tone="success">Vos modifications sont enregistrées.</z-alert>
<z-alert tone="danger" dismissible>Le paiement a été refusé.</z-alert>
```

Attributes:
- `tone` ("main" | "complement" | "soft" | "success" | "danger") [main | complement | soft | success | danger] — The kind of message — drives colour and, for danger, the live politeness.
- `dismissible` (boolean) — Adds a × ; closes on click (on the ×) or Delete/Backspace when focused.

Events: `zoe:dismiss` — Cancelable — fired before closing. preventDefault() to handle it yourself. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-alert:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The banner surface — carries the tone.
- `infos` — What informs — icon + message.
- infos › `icon` (optional) — Optional status icon.
- infos › `label` — The message.

JS API:
- `dismiss()` : Promise<void> — Closes the alert: fires cancelable `zoe:dismiss`, then plays `exit` and removes the node.

Files: doc: components/z-alert/z-alert.doc.md · demo: components/z-alert/z-alert.demo.html

### <z-avatar>

An identity chip — an image if given, otherwise the initials. role=img with an alt from name. Inherits tone/size.

```html
<z-avatar name="Ada Lovelace">AL</z-avatar>
<z-avatar name="Grace Hopper" src="/img/grace.jpg"></z-avatar>
<z-avatar name="Inconnu" size="l" tone="soft">?</z-avatar>
```

Attributes:
- `src` (url) — Image URL — set as the host's background (no injected <img>).
- `name` (string) — The person/thing shown — becomes the accessible alt (role=img + aria-label).
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-avatar:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The disc — carries the image or the tone.
- `label` — The initials (fallback when there's no image).

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-avatar--background__color`, `--z-avatar__image`

JS API:
- `src` : string — The image URL (mirrors the attribute).
- `name` : string — The accessible name (mirrors the attribute).

Files: doc: components/z-avatar/z-avatar.doc.md · demo: components/z-avatar/z-avatar.demo.html

### <z-avatar-group>

A stack of overlapping z-avatar, each ringed in the page colour to stand out. On hover, the avatar lifts and comes to the front. Nothing injected.

```html
<z-avatar-group max="3">
  <z-avatar name="Ada Lovelace">AL</z-avatar>
  <z-avatar name="Grace Hopper">GH</z-avatar>
  <z-avatar name="Margaret Hamilton">MH</z-avatar>
  <z-avatar name="4 autres personnes" tone="soft">+4</z-avatar>
</z-avatar-group>
```

Attributes:
- `max` (number) — Author's guide: past this many faces, add a final <z-avatar>+N</z-avatar> yourself (no node is generated).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-avatar-group:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-avatar-group__overlap` — How much each avatar slides over the previous one (negative margin).
- `--z-avatar-group__ring` — Thickness of the separating ring (page colour).
- `--z-avatar-group__lift` — How high the hovered avatar rises.

Files: doc: components/z-avatar-group/z-avatar-group.doc.md · demo: components/z-avatar-group/z-avatar-group.demo.html

### <z-badge>

A status/count pill — inherits z-element's tone & size variants, painted by the skin. Almost zero code: the frozen socle does the work.

```html
<z-badge>Nouveau</z-badge>
<z-badge tone="danger">3</z-badge>
<z-badge tone="success" size="s">payé</z-badge>
```

Attributes:
- `tone` ("main" | "complement" | "soft" | "success" | "danger") [main | complement | soft | success | danger] — Importance/colour, from the socle variant.
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant (everything follows in em).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-badge:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The pill surface — carries tone and effects.
- `infos` — What informs — the badge's text/number.
- infos › `label` — Your text.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-badge--background__border`, `--z-badge--background__color`

Files: doc: components/z-badge/z-badge.doc.md · demo: components/z-badge/z-badge.demo.html

### <z-breadcrumb>

A breadcrumb trail — you write the links, Zoé adds the meaning (nav + label) and the « › » separators in CSS. Nothing injected.

```html
<z-breadcrumb label="Vous êtes ici">
  <a href="/">Accueil</a>
  <a href="/boutique">Boutique</a>
  <span aria-current="page">Chaussures</span>
</z-breadcrumb>
```

Attributes:
- `label` (string) — The accessible name of the navigation (defaults to « Fil d'Ariane »).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-breadcrumb:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-breadcrumb__separator` — The glyph drawn between links (default « › »).
- `--z-breadcrumb__gap` — Space around each separator.

### <z-button>

A button — inherits all z-element states, skinnable by themes.

```html
<z-button>Envoyer</z-button>
<z-button tone="soft">Annuler</z-button>
<z-button loading>Chargement…</z-button>
<form>
  <z-button type="submit">Valider</z-button>
  <z-button type="reset" tone="soft">Réinitialiser</z-button>
</form>
```

Attributes:
- `type` ("submit" | "reset" | "button") [submit | reset | button] — What it does inside a form: submit (default), reset, or nothing.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: blocks interaction.
- `loading` (boolean) — Loading (skeleton sweep, not clickable).
- `error` (boolean) — Error (danger border + shake).
- `success` (boolean) — Valid (success border).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-button:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The button's surface and outline — a piece of its own, it can move without the text.
- `infos` — What informs — moved, hidden or animated as one block.
- infos › `icon` (optional) — Optional, before the label.
- infos › `label` — Your text.
- `contact` — What receives the gesture — covers (and may overflow) the component, invisible.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-button--background__border`, `--z-button--background__border-current`, `--z-button--background__color`, `--z-button--background__color-current`, `--z-button--contact__bleed`, `--z-button--halo__color`, `--z-button--icon__color`, `--z-button--label__color-current`

JS API:
- `type` : "submit" | "reset" | "button" — What it does inside a form (mirrors the attribute; default submit).

Files: doc: components/z-button/z-button.doc.md · demo: components/z-button/z-button.demo.html · lab: components/z-button/z-button.lab.html

### <z-card>

A surface card holding free content — inherits tone & size; optionally interactive (hover + clickable, role=button).

```html
<z-card>
  <h3>Titre de la carte</h3>
  <p>Contenu libre : texte, images, autres composants.</p>
</z-card>
<z-card interactive tone="soft">Toute la carte est cliquable.</z-card>
```

Attributes:
- `interactive` (boolean) — The whole card reacts to hover (elevation + accent border) and becomes focusable/clickable — role=button, Enter/Space fire a click.
- `tone` ("main" | "complement" | "soft" | "success" | "danger") [main | complement | soft | success | danger] — Importance/colour, from the socle variant.
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant (everything follows in em).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-card:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The card surface — radius, border, elevation.
- `media` (optional) — Optional visual at the head of the card (image, banner).
- `infos` — What informs — the card's content block.
- infos › `label` — The card's title/text.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-card--background__border`, `--z-card--background__color`

JS API:
- `interactive` : boolean — Mirrors the `interactive` attribute.

Files: doc: components/z-card/z-card.doc.md · demo: components/z-card/z-card.demo.html

### <z-checkbox>

A checkbox — inherits all z-element states, marker + label anatomy, painted by the skin.

```html
<z-checkbox name="cgu" required>J'accepte les conditions</z-checkbox>
<z-checkbox name="lettre" value="hebdo" current>Recevoir la lettre</z-checkbox>
<z-checkbox indeterminate>Tout cocher</z-checkbox>
```

Attributes:
- `current` (boolean) — Checked: a durable selection set by the component (click / Space).
- `indeterminate` (boolean) — Neither checked nor unchecked — the state of a 'check all' box whose children disagree. Any click resolves it to checked.
- `name` (string) — Form field name.
- `value` (string) — What is submitted when checked (default: "on", like the native input).
- `required` (boolean) — The form is invalid until this box is checked.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: blocks interaction.
- `error` (boolean) — Invalid (e.g. required and unchecked).
- `success` (boolean) — Valid.

Events: `change` — Emitted when the checked state toggles. Read `.checked`. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-checkbox:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `indeterminate`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The backdrop of the whole line — usually transparent, it carries effects.
- `marker` — The box itself (its surface).
- marker › `ring` — The box outline — animatable on its own (it can spin, dash…).
- marker › `dot` — The mark that appears once checked.
- `infos` — What informs — moved, hidden or animated as one block.
- infos › `icon` (optional) — Optional, before the label.
- infos › `label` — Your text.
- `contact` — What receives the gesture — covers (and may overflow) the component, invisible.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-checkbox--background__bleed`, `--z-checkbox--background__color`, `--z-checkbox--background__radius`, `--z-checkbox--contact__bleed`, `--z-checkbox--dot__bar-height`, `--z-checkbox--dot__bar-scale`, `--z-checkbox--dot__color`, `--z-checkbox--dot__radius`, `--z-checkbox--dot__size`, `--z-checkbox--halo__color`, `--z-checkbox--icon__color`, `--z-checkbox--label__emphasis`, `--z-checkbox--label__weight`, `--z-checkbox--marker__background`, `--z-checkbox--marker__background-checked`, `--z-checkbox--marker__radius`, `--z-checkbox--marker__size`, `--z-checkbox--ring__color`, `--z-checkbox--ring__color-checked`, `--z-checkbox__gap`

JS API:
- `checked` : boolean — Checked or not — mirrors `current`. Setting it never clears `indeterminate`.
- `indeterminate` : boolean — The third value (aria-checked=mixed).
- `value` : string — What is submitted when checked (default "on").

Files: doc: components/z-checkbox/z-checkbox.doc.md · demo: components/z-checkbox/z-checkbox.demo.html · lab: components/z-checkbox/z-checkbox.lab.html

### <z-checkbox-group>

A group of z-checkbox: a list value, a 'check all' master, 'at least one' required, one name for FormData.

```html
<z-checkbox-group name="topics" required>
  <span part="label">Vos centres d'intérêt</span>
  <z-checkbox part="all">Tout cocher</z-checkbox>
  <z-checkbox value="design">Design</z-checkbox>
  <z-checkbox value="code" current>Code</z-checkbox>
  <z-checkbox value="motion">Motion</z-checkbox>
</z-checkbox-group>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (string) — Space-separated values to preselect (honoured once, only if no box is checked by hand); then kept up to date by the group.
- `name` (string) — Given to every box that has none: the values are submitted under this name.
- `required` (boolean) — At least one box must be checked, or the form refuses to submit.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disables the whole group — descended on every box and the master.
- `error` (boolean) — The requirement is not met and the form refused to submit (posed by the group, cleared by the next check).
- `success` (boolean) — The requirement is met, after a gesture.

Events: `change` — Bubbles from the toggled box (the group's `.value` is already up to date) — or is emitted by the group itself when the master toggles everything. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-checkbox-group:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `label` (optional) — The group's title, any native tag — it names the group (aria-labelledby).
- `all` (optional) — The master z-checkbox: toggles every box, reflects the list (checked / indeterminate / none). Never submitted, never counted.

CSS variables:
- `--z-checkbox-group__count` — Posed by the group: how many boxes are checked (an integer, for counter()).
- `--z-checkbox-group__total` — Posed by the group: how many boxes it holds (master excluded).

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-checkbox-group--label__color`, `--z-checkbox-group--label__font-size`, `--z-checkbox-group--rule__color`, `--z-checkbox-group__align`, `--z-checkbox-group__direction`, `--z-checkbox-group__gap`

JS API:
- `value` : string[] — The checked values, in DOM order. Set it with an array or a space-separated string — silently (no `change`).
- `checkboxes` : Element[] — The z-checkbox of this group — not the master, not those of a nested group.
- `all` : Element | null — The master box ([part=all]), if any.
- `count` : number — How many boxes are checked.

Files: doc: components/z-checkbox-group/z-checkbox-group.doc.md · demo: components/z-checkbox-group/z-checkbox-group.demo.html

### <z-code>

Displays code as written — a block by default (pre-like, scrolls horizontally) or inline with `inline` (a monospace chip). No syntax highlighting, nothing injected.

```html
<z-code>npm run dev
# http://localhost:5173</z-code>
<p>Installez avec <z-code inline>npm install</z-code>.</p>
```

Attributes:
- `inline` (boolean) — Render as an inline chip in a line of text instead of a block.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-code:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The sunken code surface.
- `infos` — What informs — the code itself.
- infos › `label` — Your code text.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-code--background__border`, `--z-code--background__color`, `--z-code--background__radius`, `--z-code--infos__color`

JS API:
- `inline` : boolean — Mirrors the `inline` attribute.

Files: doc: components/z-code/z-code.doc.md · demo: components/z-code/z-code.demo.html

### <z-dialog>

A modal box on the native <dialog> — adds states, animated open/close, declarative triggers (commandfor/command) and light-dismiss.

```html
<z-dialog id="confirm" light-dismiss>
  <dialog>
    <header part="header"><h2>Supprimer ce fichier ?</h2></header>
    <p part="body">Cette action est définitive.</p>
    <footer part="footer">
      <z-button type="button" command="close" tone="soft">Annuler</z-button>
      <z-button type="button" command="close" value="delete" tone="danger">Supprimer</z-button>
    </footer>
  </dialog>
</z-dialog>
<z-button type="button" commandfor="confirm" command="show-modal">Supprimer…</z-button>
```

Attributes:
- `open` (boolean) — Open (modal). The source of truth: set by the component, settable by hand.
- `light-dismiss` (boolean) — A click on the backdrop closes the box (through `cancel`, like Escape).
- `placement` ("center" | "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right") [center | top | bottom | left | right] — Where the box sits — center (default) pops, the four edges slide in from their side.

Events: `open` — Emitted once shown (bubbles). · `close` — Emitted once closed, after the exit animation (bubbles). detail: { returnValue }. · `cancel` — Escape, light-dismiss or request-close (bubbles, cancelable): preventDefault() keeps the box open. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-dialog:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `open`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `header` (optional) — The title row — your heading, and a close button if you want one.
- `body` (optional) — The content.
- `footer` (optional) — The actions — laid out in a row, pushed to the right.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-dialog--backdrop__background`, `--z-dialog--footer__border-color`, `--z-dialog--footer__gap`, `--z-dialog--header__border-color`, `--z-dialog--header__font-size`, `--z-dialog__background`, `--z-dialog__border-color`, `--z-dialog__color`, `--z-dialog__gap`, `--z-dialog__offset`, `--z-dialog__padding`, `--z-dialog__radius`, `--z-dialog__shadow`, `--z-dialog__width`

JS API:
- `show()` : void — Opens modally (dialog.showModal()) and plays `enter`. Same as setting the `open` attribute.
- `close(returnValue?)` : Promise<void> — Plays `exit`, THEN calls dialog.close(returnValue). Resolves once closed; fires `close`.
- `requestClose()` : void — Closes the way Escape does: fires cancelable `cancel` first — preventDefault() keeps the dialog open.
- `toggle()` : void — Opens if closed, closes if open.
- `open` : boolean — Open or closed — mirrors the attribute. Setting it goes through show() / close(), so it animates.
- `returnValue` : string — The native dialog's returnValue — the `value` of the trigger that closed it.
- `placement` : "center" | "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" — Where the box sits (mirrors the attribute; default center).
- `dialog` : HTMLDialogElement | null — The author's native <dialog> inside.

Files: doc: components/z-dialog/z-dialog.doc.md · demo: components/z-dialog/z-dialog.demo.html

### <z-disclosure>

A disclosure (title → collapsible content) — inherits z-element states, accessible (aria-expanded/controls, inert when closed), animatable.

```html
<z-disclosure open>
  <z-layer part="label">Ce que Zoé garde natif</z-layer>
  <z-layer part="panel">Titres, paragraphes, liens — lus par les moteurs de recherche.</z-layer>
</z-disclosure>
```

Attributes:
- `open` (boolean) — Open: reveals the panel.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: the label no longer opens or closes (pointer and keyboard).

Events: `toggle` — Emitted when it opens or closes. Read `.open`. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-disclosure:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `open`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `label` — The trigger — a button that reveals/hides the panel.
- `panel` — The collapsible content.

JS API:
- `open` : boolean — Open or closed — mirrors the attribute.
- `toggle()` : void — Opens or closes, and fires `toggle`.

Files: doc: components/z-disclosure/z-disclosure.doc.md · demo: components/z-disclosure/z-disclosure.demo.html

### <z-divider>

A separator — a plain rule, or two rules framing a centred label. role=separator + aria-orientation.

```html
<z-divider></z-divider>
<z-divider>ou</z-divider>
<z-divider orientation="vertical"></z-divider>
```

Attributes:
- `orientation` ("horizontal" | "vertical") [horizontal | vertical] — Direction of the rule: horizontal (default) or vertical (a short 1em stroke).
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant: the label and the vertical stroke's length follow in em; the thickness stays --z-border-width.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-divider:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `infos` — What informs — the centred label, if any.
- infos › `label` (optional) — Optional centred text (the two rules frame it).

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-divider__color`

JS API:
- `orientation` : "horizontal" | "vertical" — Mirrors the attribute.

### <z-drawer>

A modal side panel — a z-dialog glued to an edge: full height, slides in from its side. Same API, same triggers.

```html
<z-drawer id="menu" light-dismiss>
  <dialog>
    <header part="header">
      <h2>Menu</h2>
      <z-button type="button" command="close" tone="soft">Fermer</z-button>
    </header>
    <nav part="body">
      <a href="#">Accueil</a>
      <a href="#">Catalogue</a>
      <a href="#">Contact</a>
    </nav>
  </dialog>
</z-drawer>
<z-button type="button" commandfor="menu" command="show-modal">Menu</z-button>
```

Attributes:
- `open` (boolean) — Open (modal). The source of truth: set by the component, settable by hand.
- `light-dismiss` (boolean) — A click on the backdrop closes the box (through `cancel`, like Escape).
- `placement` ("right" | "left" | "top" | "bottom") [right | left | top | bottom] — The edge the panel is glued to (default right).

Events: `open` — Emitted once shown (bubbles). · `close` — Emitted once closed, after the exit animation (bubbles). detail: { returnValue }. · `cancel` — Escape, light-dismiss or request-close (bubbles, cancelable): preventDefault() keeps the box open. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-drawer:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `open`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `header` (optional) — The title row — your heading, and a close button if you want one.
- `body` (optional) — The content.
- `footer` (optional) — The actions — laid out in a row, pushed to the right.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-drawer__height`, `--z-drawer__width`

JS API:
- `show()` : void — Opens modally (dialog.showModal()) and plays `enter`. Same as setting the `open` attribute.
- `close(returnValue?)` : Promise<void> — Plays `exit`, THEN calls dialog.close(returnValue). Resolves once closed; fires `close`.
- `requestClose()` : void — Closes the way Escape does: fires cancelable `cancel` first — preventDefault() keeps the dialog open.
- `toggle()` : void — Opens if closed, closes if open.
- `open` : boolean — Open or closed — mirrors the attribute. Setting it goes through show() / close(), so it animates.
- `returnValue` : string — The native dialog's returnValue — the `value` of the trigger that closed it.
- `placement` : "right" | "left" | "top" | "bottom" — The edge the panel is glued to (mirrors the attribute; default right).
- `dialog` : HTMLDialogElement | null — The author's native <dialog> inside.

Files: doc: components/z-drawer/z-drawer.doc.md · demo: components/z-drawer/z-drawer.demo.html

### <z-field>

A form field around a NATIVE control: links label, hint and error, mirrors its validity into error/success, poses filled. Nothing replaced, nothing injected.

```html
<z-field>
  <label>Adresse e-mail</label>
  <input type="email" name="email" required placeholder="vous@exemple.fr">
  <small part="hint">Nous ne la partagerons jamais.</small>
  <small part="error"></small>
</z-field>
```

Attributes:
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disables the field: propagated to the native control (and removed with it).
- `counter` (boolean) — Writes « length / maxlength » at the end of [part=hint], in pure CSS (the hint must exist, empty is fine).
- `filled` (boolean) — Posed by the field: the control has a non-empty value (for a floating label in CSS).
- `error` (boolean) — Posed by the field once judged and invalid — you may also set it by hand with your own [part=error] text.
- `success` (boolean) — Posed by the field once judged, valid and non-empty.

Events: `input` — The native control's — it bubbles through the field untouched. · `change` — The native control's — it bubbles through the field untouched. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change (error, success, filled…). detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-field:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `filled`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `label` — A native <label> — linked to the control (for/id) by the field.
- `control` — The native <input>, <textarea> or <select>, direct child — the only required piece, and the single source of truth (name, required, type, maxlength live on it).
- `hint` (optional) — Help text under the control (aria-describedby); the counter is written at its end.
- `error` (optional) — The error message — shown only in :state(error). Left empty, the field writes the browser's validationMessage in it.

CSS variables:
- `--z-field__length` — Posed by the field: the value's length (an integer, for counter()).
- `--z-field__max` — Posed by the field: the control's maxlength (0 when none).

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-field--control__background`, `--z-field--control__border-color`, `--z-field--control__color`, `--z-field--control__font-size`, `--z-field--control__padding`, `--z-field--control__radius`, `--z-field--counter__color`, `--z-field--error__color`, `--z-field--hint__color`, `--z-field--hint__font-size`, `--z-field--label__color`, `--z-field--label__font-size`, `--z-field--label__font-weight`, `--z-field__gap`, `--z-field__inline-size`

JS API:
- `control` : HTMLElement | null — The native <input>, <textarea> or <select> the field wraps (read-only).
- `valid` : boolean — The control's native validity, right now (read-only).
- `validate()` : boolean — Judges the field now — poses error/success and the message — and returns its validity.

Files: doc: components/z-field/z-field.doc.md · demo: components/z-field/z-field.demo.html

### <z-kbd>

A keyboard key cap — pure display, monospace, bordered with a subtle key relief. Inherits size.

```html
<p>Appuyez sur <z-kbd>Ctrl</z-kbd> + <z-kbd>K</z-kbd> pour chercher.</p>
```

Attributes:
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant (everything follows in em).

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-kbd:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The key cap surface — border and relief.
- `infos` — What informs — the key's text.
- infos › `label` — The key legend (e.g. "Ctrl").

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-kbd--background__border`, `--z-kbd--background__color`

Files: doc: components/z-kbd/z-kbd.doc.md · demo: components/z-kbd/z-kbd.demo.html

### <z-menu>

An actions menu (ARIA menu button) on top of z-popover — roles, roving focus, arrow keys, type-ahead; activating an item fires cancelable `select` then closes.

```html
<z-menu>
  <z-button part="trigger" type="button">Actions ▾</z-button>
  <div part="panel">
    <button part="item" value="rename">Renommer</button>
    <button part="item" value="duplicate">Dupliquer</button>
    <hr part="separator">
    <button part="item" value="delete" tone="danger">Supprimer</button>
  </div>
</z-menu>
```

Attributes:
- `open` (boolean) — Open: the panel is shown. The source of truth — set by click, show()/hide(), and synced when the browser closes it (light-dismiss, Escape).
- `placement` ("bottom" | "top" | "left" | "right") [bottom | top | left | right] — The side of the trigger the panel opens on (default bottom). Flipped to the opposite side when it would overflow the viewport.
- `align` ("start" | "center" | "end") [start | center | end] — Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with (default start).
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: the trigger no longer opens it.

Events: `select` — Emitted when an item is activated (click, Enter, Space). Bubbles, cancelable: preventDefault() keeps the menu open. detail: { value, item } — value is the item's `value` attribute, or its text. · `toggle` — Emitted on every open/close, whoever caused it (click, API, light-dismiss, Escape). Bubbles. detail: { open }. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-menu:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `open`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `trigger` — The menu button — any focusable element. Gets aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, aria-controls.
- `panel` — The list of actions (role=menu) — anchored, in the top layer, animated by z-popover.
- panel › `item` — One action (role=menuitem, tabindex=-1) — a <button> or an <a href>. `value` names it in `select`; `disabled` / aria-disabled skips it.
- panel › `separator` (optional) — A rule between two groups of actions (role=separator).

CSS variables:
- `--z-popover__x` — Set on the panel by the inherited z-popover anchoring — its left edge in the viewport, a bare number of px.
- `--z-popover__y` — Set on the panel by the inherited z-popover anchoring — its top edge in the viewport, a bare number of px.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-menu--item__background`, `--z-menu--item__background-over`, `--z-menu--item__color`, `--z-menu--item__color-over`, `--z-menu--item__gap`, `--z-menu--item__padding`, `--z-menu--item__radius`, `--z-menu--separator__color`, `--z-menu--separator__margin`, `--z-menu__min-width`, `--z-menu__padding`, `--z-menu__width`

JS API:
- `open` : boolean — Open or closed — mirrors the attribute.
- `placement` : "bottom" | "top" | "left" | "right" — The requested side (mirrors the attribute; default bottom). The effective side is `data-placement` on the panel.
- `align` : "start" | "center" | "end" — Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with (mirrors the attribute; default start).
- `trigger · panel` : Element | null — The `[part=trigger]` and `[part=panel]` children, resolved on connect.
- `show()` : void — Opens (sets `open`).
- `hide()` : void — Closes (clears `open`); focus returns to the trigger if it was inside.
- `toggle()` : void — Opens or closes.
- `items` : Element[] — The `[part=item]` elements of THIS menu (not those of a nested menu), disabled ones included.

Files: doc: components/z-menu/z-menu.doc.md · demo: components/z-menu/z-menu.demo.html

### <z-meter>

A gauge (role=meter): a scalar measurement within a range, coloured by low/high/optimum thresholds. Not a progress bar — it shows a state, not an advance.

```html
<z-meter value="72"></z-meter>
<z-meter value="15" low="20" high="80" optimum="100"></z-meter>
<z-meter value="3" max="5"></z-meter>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (number) — The measured amount (min…max).
- `min` (number) — Lower bound (default 0).
- `max` (number) — Upper bound (default 100).
- `low` (number) — Below this, the value is in the low segment.
- `high` (number) — Above this, the value is in the high segment.
- `optimum` (number) — Where the ideal sits — a value in the same zone is `optimum` (painted with the tone) instead of low/high.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-meter:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `low`, `high`, `optimum`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The track (the empty rail).
- `marker` — The fill — its width is the measurement, its colour follows the threshold.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-meter--fill__color`, `--z-meter--track__color`, `--z-meter--track__height`, `--z-meter__fill`, `--z-meter__value`

JS API:
- `value` : number — The measured amount.
- `min · max` : number — The bounds (mirror the attributes).

Files: doc: components/z-meter/z-meter.doc.md · demo: components/z-meter/z-meter.demo.html

### <z-pagination>

SEO-correct pagination: you write real links, Zoé poses the meaning, the current page, the bounds, the window and the keyboard. Nothing generated.

```html
<z-pagination page="3" siblings="1" label="Pages des résultats">
  <a part="prev" href="?p=2">Précédent</a>
  <a href="?p=1">1</a>
  <a href="?p=2">2</a>
  <a href="?p=3">3</a>
  <a href="?p=4">4</a>
  <a href="?p=5">5</a>
  <a href="?p=12">12</a>
  <a part="next" href="?p=4">Suivant</a>
</z-pagination>
```

Attributes:
- `page` (number) — The current page: the link whose text is this number is marked current. Absent, the link carrying aria-current="page" is, else the first.
- `siblings` (number) — How many pages stay visible on each side of the current one (default 1). Farther ones get `far`, the first and last always stay.
- `label` (string) — The accessible name of the navigation (default « Pagination »).
- `disabled` (boolean) — Freezes the whole navigation.

Events: `change` — A page, prev or next was clicked. detail: { page }. Cancelable: preventDefault() and the component poses `page` itself instead of letting the link navigate. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-pagination:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `page` — A page link — any direct child without `part` (writing part="page" is allowed). Its text is its number. The current one carries aria-current + current; hidden ones carry far; one preceded by a hole carries gap.
- `prev` (optional) — The « previous » link — disabled (aria-disabled + disabled) on the first page.
- `next` (optional) — The « next » link — disabled on the last page.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-pagination--ellipsis__color`, `--z-pagination--ellipsis__size`, `--z-pagination--page__background`, `--z-pagination--page__background-current`, `--z-pagination--page__border-color`, `--z-pagination--page__color`, `--z-pagination--page__color-current`, `--z-pagination--page__padding`, `--z-pagination--page__radius`, `--z-pagination--page__size`, `--z-pagination__gap`

JS API:
- `page` : number — The current page number. Setting it moves the current mark and the window (no `change`).
- `pages` : Element[] — The page links, in order — direct children without `part` (or part=page).
- `last` : number — The last page: the largest number read in the links (0 when none).

Files: doc: components/z-pagination/z-pagination.doc.md · demo: components/z-pagination/z-pagination.demo.html

### <z-popover>

A floating panel anchored to its trigger — native Popover API (top layer, light-dismiss, Escape), JS anchoring that flips when it overflows, animated in and out.

```html
<z-popover placement="bottom">
  <z-button part="trigger" type="button">Options</z-button>
  <div part="panel">
    <p>Contenu libre.</p>
  </div>
</z-popover>
```

Attributes:
- `open` (boolean) — Open: the panel is shown. The source of truth — set by click, show()/hide(), and synced when the browser closes it (light-dismiss, Escape).
- `placement` ("bottom" | "top" | "left" | "right") [bottom | top | left | right] — The side of the trigger the panel opens on (default bottom). Flipped to the opposite side when it would overflow the viewport.
- `align` ("start" | "center" | "end") [start | center | end] — Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with (default start).
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: the trigger no longer opens it.

Events: `toggle` — Emitted on every open/close, whoever caused it (click, API, light-dismiss, Escape). Bubbles. detail: { open }. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-popover:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `open`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `trigger` — What opens it — any focusable element (a z-button, a button). Gets aria-expanded + aria-controls.
- `panel` — What opens — your content. Gets popover="auto", an id, and data-placement (the effective side).

CSS variables:
- `--z-popover__x` — Set by z-popover on the panel — its left edge in the viewport, a bare number of px (the CSS multiplies: `calc(var(--z-popover__x) * 1px)`).
- `--z-popover__y` — Set by z-popover on the panel — its top edge in the viewport, a bare number of px.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-popover--panel__translate`, `--z-popover__background`, `--z-popover__border-color`, `--z-popover__color`, `--z-popover__max-height`, `--z-popover__max-width`, `--z-popover__offset`, `--z-popover__padding`, `--z-popover__radius`, `--z-popover__shadow`, `--z-popover__travel`, `--z-popover__width`

JS API:
- `open` : boolean — Open or closed — mirrors the attribute.
- `placement` : "bottom" | "top" | "left" | "right" — The requested side (mirrors the attribute; default bottom). The effective side is `data-placement` on the panel.
- `align` : "start" | "center" | "end" — Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with (mirrors the attribute; default start).
- `trigger · panel` : Element | null — The `[part=trigger]` and `[part=panel]` children, resolved on connect.
- `show()` : void — Opens (sets `open`).
- `hide()` : void — Closes (clears `open`); focus returns to the trigger if it was inside.
- `toggle()` : void — Opens or closes.

Files: doc: components/z-popover/z-popover.doc.md · demo: components/z-popover/z-popover.demo.html

### <z-progress>

A progress bar — inherits z-element states + tone/size, painted by the skin. value/max → a percentage the CSS draws.

```html
<z-progress value="40"></z-progress>

```

- `value` (number) — Current amount (0…max).
- `max` (number) — The total (default 100).
- `indeterminate` (boolean) — Unknown amount — a sweep animates, aria-valuenow is dropped.
- `tone` ("main" | "complement" | "soft" | "success" | "danger") [main | complement | soft | success | danger] — Fill colour, from the socle variant.
- `size` ("xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl") [xs | s | m | l | xl] — Size factor, from the socle variant.

Events: `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-progress:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`, `indeterminate`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The track (the empty rail).
- `marker` — The fill — its width is the progress.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-progress--fill__color`, `--z-progress--track__color`, `--z-progress--track__height`, `--z-progress__value`

JS API:
- `value` : number — Current amount (mirrors the attribute).
- `max` : number — The total (default 100).
- `indeterminate` : boolean — Unknown amount — a sweep animates.

Files: doc: components/z-progress/z-progress.doc.md · demo: components/z-progress/z-progress.demo.html

### <z-radio>

A radio button — z-element states, marker + label anatomy, selects but never unselects itself.

```html
<z-radio value="fr">Français</z-radio>
<z-radio value="en" current>English</z-radio>
<z-radio value="es" disabled>Español</z-radio>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (string) — The value this radio carries — read by z-radio-group.
- `current` (boolean) — Selected: a durable selection set by the component (click / Space / Enter).
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: blocks interaction.
- `error` (boolean) — Invalid (e.g. a required choice is missing).
- `success` (boolean) — Valid.

Events: `change` — Emitted when this radio becomes selected. Read `.checked` / `.value`. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-radio:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The backdrop of the whole line — usually transparent, it carries effects.
- `marker` — The round itself (its surface).
- marker › `ring` — Its outline — animatable on its own.
- marker › `dot` — The mark that appears once chosen.
- `infos` — What informs — moved, hidden or animated as one block.
- infos › `icon` (optional) — Optional, before the label.
- infos › `label` — Your text.
- `contact` — What receives the gesture — covers (and may overflow) the component, invisible.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-radio--background__bleed`, `--z-radio--background__color`, `--z-radio--background__radius`, `--z-radio--contact__bleed`, `--z-radio--dot__color`, `--z-radio--dot__radius`, `--z-radio--dot__size`, `--z-radio--halo__color`, `--z-radio--icon__color`, `--z-radio--label__emphasis`, `--z-radio--label__weight`, `--z-radio--marker__background`, `--z-radio--marker__background-checked`, `--z-radio--marker__radius`, `--z-radio--marker__size`, `--z-radio--ring__color`, `--z-radio--ring__color-checked`, `--z-radio__gap`

JS API:
- `checked` : boolean — Chosen or not — mirrors `current`. Only code can set it to false.
- `value` : string — The `value` attribute, or the label text when absent.

Files: doc: components/z-radio/z-radio.doc.md · demo: components/z-radio/z-radio.demo.html

### <z-radio-group>

A group of z-radio: single choice, arrow-key navigation, roving tabindex, one value.

```html
<z-radio-group value="en" name="lang">
  <z-radio value="fr">Français</z-radio>
  <z-radio value="en">English</z-radio>
  <z-radio value="es">Español</z-radio>
</z-radio-group>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (string) — The selected radio's value — set it to preselect, read it to know the choice.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disables the whole group.
- `error` (boolean) — The group's choice is invalid (e.g. required and empty).
- `success` (boolean) — The group's choice is valid.

Events: `change` — Bubbles from the chosen radio; the group's `.value` is already up to date. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-radio-group:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

CSS variables:
- `--z-radio-group__gap` — Space between the radios.
- `--z-radio-group__direction` — Layout direction: column (default) or row.
- `--z-radio-group__align` — Cross-axis alignment of the choices.

JS API:
- `value` : string — The chosen radio's value (empty when none). Setting it selects without firing `change`.
- `radios` : Element[] — The z-radio of this group (not those of a nested group).
- `selected` : Element | null — The chosen radio.

Files: doc: components/z-radio-group/z-radio-group.doc.md · demo: components/z-radio-group/z-radio-group.demo.html · lab: components/z-radio-group/z-radio-group.lab.html

### <z-rating>

A star rating — a slider from 0 to max, set by click or keyboard, painted by the skin.

```html
<z-rating value="3"></z-rating>
<z-rating value="4" max="5" name="note"></z-rating>
<z-rating value="2" readonly></z-rating>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (number) — Current rating, an integer in [0, max]. Clamped and rounded.
- `max` (number) — Number of stars (default 5).
- `readonly` (boolean) — Shown but not editable — a rating you display.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disabled: blocks interaction.
- `name` (string) — Form field name.
- `required` (boolean) — The form is invalid while the rating is 0.

Events: `input` — Emitted on every value change, including during keyboard steps. Read `.value`. · `change` — Emitted once the gesture is over (click done, key up). · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-rating:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `background` — The backdrop of the row — usually transparent, it carries effects.
- `marker` — The stars: an empty row with a filled row clipped to the value.
- `contact` — What receives the gesture — covers the row, invisible.

CSS variables:
- `--z-rating__value` — The filled part, as a percentage — the CSS clips the full layer to it.
- `--z-rating__stars` — A string of `max` glyphs, written by content: without any injected node.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-rating--empty__color`, `--z-rating--full__color`, `--z-rating__gap`, `--z-rating__size`

JS API:
- `value` : number — The rating, an integer in [0, max].
- `max` : number — Number of stars (default 5).
- `readonly` : boolean — Shown but not editable.

Files: doc: components/z-rating/z-rating.doc.md · demo: components/z-rating/z-rating.demo.html

### <z-segmented>

A segmented control: single choice among 2–5 options, with an indicator that slides under the current one.

```html
<z-segmented value="mois">
  <button part="segment" value="jour">Jour</button>
  <button part="segment" value="mois">Mois</button>
  <button part="segment" value="an">Année</button>
</z-segmented>
```

Attributes:
- `value` (string) — The chosen segment's value — set it to preselect, read it to know the choice.
- `disabled` (boolean) — Disables the whole control.

Events: `change` — Emitted when the choice changes. detail: { value }; also read `.value`. · `z-state` — Emitted on every state change. detail: { states, changed, on }.

States (`z-segmented:state(…)`): `default`, `over`, `press`, `release`, `releaseOut`, `drag`, `focus`, `enter`, `exit`, `current`, `select`, `unselect`, `loading`, `disabled`, `error`, `success`

Layers (`<z-layer part="…">`, author-written):
- `segment` — One option — the author writes as many as needed (2 to 5). Carries a `value`.

CSS variables:
- `--z-segmented__x` — Left offset (px) of the current segment — the indicator slides to it.
- `--z-segmented__w` — Width (px) of the current segment — the indicator matches it.

Skin tokens it reads (`--z-{component}[--{part}]__{property}`): `--z-segmented--background__color`, `--z-segmented--indicator__color`, `--z-segmented--indicator__shadow`, `--z-segmented--segment__ink`, `--z-segmented--segment__pad`, `--z-segmented__gap`, `--z-segmented__pad`

JS API:
- `value` : string — The chosen segment's value. Setting it selects without firing `change`.
- `segments` : Element[] — The `[part=segment]` children.
- `selected` : Element | null — The current segment.
